title: GND ORM conceptual model (full D-01 vocabulary)
description: Draft 2020-12 meta-schema for model.orm.yaml — the complete Halpin ORM 2 constraint vocabulary: uniqueness (internal/external), mandatory, mandatory-disjunctive, value (enum/range/ranges/role-scope hybrid), frequency (internal/external), ring (all variants), subset, equality, exclusion, exclusive-or, value-comparison (intra- and cross-fact-type), cardinality (object/role), subtype-partition, textual — plus GND's conditional guarded extension and subtyping on object types. Constraint placement follows the source spec: single-fact-type constraints live inline under fact_types[].constraints; cross-fact-type and object-type-scope constraints live top-level under constraints. GND divergences from the RAI source spec: (1) `modality` is REQUIRED on every ACTIVE constraint, never defaulted (D-03); (2) rejected_proposals entries are schema-light and modality is NOT required there — they are archived proposals preserved to prevent re-proposal, not active constraints. Optional top-level `model_id` (D-06): a stable, opaque identifier for this model. A population header may declare the same field; when both are present and differ, the population was written for a different model and is rejected at load (exit 3). It is OPTIONAL for backward compatibility, compared as an opaque string, and never dereferenced to a path or opened. Version 2 (ORM+) adds one optional top-level section, `operations`: named state transitions carrying parameters, conjunctive positive-atom preconditions, create/assert/retract effects, old-versus-new dynamic value rules, and a REQUIRED, never-defaulted `frame.modality`. `operations` present implies `version: 2`, `version: 3` or `version: 4`; a version-2 document with no `operations` is behaviourally a version-1 document. Default snapshot checking ignores `operations`; explicit compiled-operation checking is defined in representation-format.md. Threat note (T-01-06): derivation_rule, textual expression, and value-comparison operands are typed as plain strings; the validator never interprets or executes them.

description.description: Optional explanation of what one instance of this object type is. Core keys are rendered, never interpreted; any other key is an extra, carried unchanged and never rendered as prose. See representation-format.md.

source_kind.description: The six provenance sources. `imported` (v2) records a claim carried in from another framework's artifact under a verbatim anchor; see provenance-and-modality.md for the required block and the D-03 default-modality row.

provenance_policy.description: The per-source provenance requirements, factored out of constraint_common so that operation-level obligations (preconditions, dynamic rules) and operations themselves carry the SAME rules by reference rather than by a second copy. Referenced in-place, so `unevaluatedProperties: false` on the referring envelope still sees every property this schema evaluates.

guarded.description: GND's conditional constraint extension: when every antecedent atom holds, the selected atom, comparison, absence, or existential consequent is required.

rejected_proposal.description: Schema-light by design: archived proposals, not active constraints — modality is NOT required here (GND D-03 divergence applies only to active constraints). Kept so future runs don't re-propose. An archived CONSTRAINT is identified by its `type`; an archived v2 OPERATION is identified by its `id` and carries no `type`. At least one of the two is therefore required, rather than `type` alone. Deliberately not exactly-one: constraints may now carry an `id` of their own, so an archived constraint legitimately supplies both.

term.description: One scalar term: a literal, a `$name` variable resolved by layer 2, or one closed exact function application. The same recursive language is used by derivation head/where and guarded comparison operands.

derivation_rule.description: An opaque string, one legacy clause, or a nonempty union of clauses. Normative semantics: gnd-orm-core/references/representation-format.md, "Derived fact types".

derivation_aggregate.description: One exact aggregate over body bindings. The contribution identity is the ordered over-binding paired with evaluated of value; layer 2 owns scope and primitive restrictions.

atom.description: One POSITIVE fact-presence atom. There is no negation, comparison, arithmetic, aggregation or disjunction in this language — a precondition is a conjunction of positive atoms and nothing else.

obligation.description: One precondition: a named conjunction of positive atoms that must hold in the pre-state. Carries its own REQUIRED modality — a verdict attaches here, not to the operation.

effect.description: One state delta. Exactly one of create / assert / retract. A step's effects apply as a SET and the intermediate invariant is checked afterwards, so `retract` plus `assert` on one fact type within one step already IS a replace — there is deliberately no `replace` primitive.

dynamic_rule.description: One old-versus-new value comparison over a functionally determined value role: the post-state value of `subject` compared to its pre-state value under `op`. Vacuous on first assignment or on retraction; `unchecked` when the subject is not provably functional.

frame.description: The frame declaration — REQUIRED on every operation and never defaulted, exactly like constraint modality (D-03). It grades the fact types this operation touches: alethic means an undeclared delta on such a fact type is a hard failure; deontic means it is a warning.

operation.description: One named state transition. The operation itself carries source/status/provenance but NO modality: modality lives on each obligation (precondition, dynamic rule, frame), which is where a verdict can attach.
